n: Paul now answers questions the Corinthians had sent him in a letter. “It is good for a man not to touch a woman” was likely their own slogan favoring celibacy; the JST frames it as their saying, which Paul goes on to qualify.

f.w: the things whereof ye wrote unto me
f.g: The Corinthians had written Paul with questions; chapters 7–16 respond to them.
A polite way of saying to abstain from sexual relations.

n: Because sexual temptation was everywhere in Corinth, each man should have his own wife and each woman her own husband. Marriage is the proper place for physical intimacy.

f.w: let every man have his own wife

n: Husband and wife owe each other affection and physical intimacy. The obligation runs equally both ways.

f.g: The kindness and marital intimacy that is owed to a spouse.

n: In marriage, neither spouse has sole say over his or her own body; each belongs to the other. Paul’s equal treatment of husband and wife was striking in his culture.

f.w: hath not power of her own body
f.g: Does not have exclusive authority over it.

n: Couples shouldn’t deprive each other, except by mutual agreement for a short time of focused fasting and prayer. Then they should come back together so Satan can’t exploit a lack of self-control.

f.g: Don’t withhold or deprive.
Lack of self-control.

n: Paul says this as a concession or allowance, not as a command.

f.g: As a concession, an allowance.

n: Paul wishes others could live as he does (apparently unmarried at the time), but recognizes each person has a different gift from God.
To the unmarried and widows, Paul says it is good to remain as he is — given the circumstances he will describe.

f.g: Some think Paul had been married earlier and was now a widower; scripture doesn’t say.

n: But if they can’t control their desires, they should marry. It is better to marry than to be consumed with passion.

f.g: Exercise self-control.
Burn with passion.

n: To married couples, Paul passes on the Lord’s own teaching: a wife should not separate from her husband.
If she does separate, she should remain unmarried or reconcile. And a husband should not divorce his wife.

f.g: Divorce.

n: For situations Jesus didn’t directly address, Paul gives his own apostolic counsel: a believing man married to an unbeliever who is willing to stay should not divorce her.

f.g: Not a quotation of Jesus’ earthly teaching, but Paul’s inspired counsel.

n: Likewise, a believing woman married to an unbelieving husband who wants to stay should not leave him.

f.g: Is not a Christian.

n: The believing spouse brings a holy influence into the home. The marriage isn’t defiled, and the children are under a sanctifying influence. A note in D&C 74 explains a related tradition about children and the law of Moses.

f.g: Set within the sphere of holy influence.

n: If the unbelieving spouse insists on leaving, let them go. The believer isn’t bound in such a case. God wants His people to live in peace.

f.g: Not enslaved or bound.

n: Who knows? By staying, a believing spouse might bring the other to Christ.
General principle: each person should live faithfully in whatever situation he was in when God called him. Paul teaches this in all the churches.

f.g: So let him live.

n: A Jewish convert shouldn’t try to hide his circumcision, and a Gentile convert shouldn’t get circumcised. Ethnic markers don’t determine standing with God.
Circumcision or not makes no difference. What matters is keeping God’s commandments.

f.w: keeping of the commandments of God

n: Each person should remain in the life situation he was in when he was called to Christ.

f.g: Here, one’s situation in life at conversion.

n: If you were a slave when converted, don’t let it trouble you — though if you can gain your freedom, take it.

f.g: Greek doulos — a slave or bond-servant. Many early Christians were slaves.

n: A slave who follows Christ is spiritually free in the Lord, while a free person who follows Christ becomes His servant. In Christ, worldly rank is turned upside down.
Christ bought you at the price of His own life. Don’t become enslaved to human opinions and masters.

f.w: Ye are bought with a price

n: Whatever your situation, remain in it with God. Faithfulness matters more than circumstances.

f.g: Stay close to God in that situation.

n: Regarding those who have never married, Paul has no direct command from the Lord, but offers his trustworthy judgment as one who received the Lord’s mercy.

f.g: Unmarried young people, especially young women of marriageable age.

n: Because of a “present distress” — perhaps persecution, famine, or the urgency of missionary work — Paul thinks it is wise to stay as one is for now.

f.g: A time of pressing difficulty in Paul’s day; the exact crisis is unknown.

n: If married, don’t seek to end it. If unmarried, don’t rush to marry during this crisis.

f.g: Free from (unmarried or released).

n: Still, marrying is not a sin. Paul only wants to spare them the added hardships married people would face in difficult times.

f.g: Practical worldly hardship.

n: Time is short. The JST shows Paul is speaking here to those called to the ministry: even married missionaries must give themselves fully to the Lord’s work while serving.

f.g: JST adds: “But I speak unto you who are called unto the ministry.”

n: Don’t let grief, joy, or possessions dominate you. Hold earthly things loosely.
Use the world without being consumed by it, because its present form is passing away.

f.w: the fashion of this world passeth away

f.g: Using it to the full, over-using.

n: Paul wants them free from anxieties. An unmarried servant can focus wholly on pleasing the Lord.

f.g: Anxiety, worry.

n: A married person must also attend to everyday responsibilities and to pleasing a spouse — a legitimate but divided focus.

f.w: how he may please his wife

n: The same is true for women: an unmarried woman can focus fully on holiness and the Lord, while a married woman must also care for her husband and home.

f.w: holy both in body and in spirit

n: Paul isn’t trying to trap or burden them, but to help them serve the Lord with undivided devotion.

f.g: A noose or trap — here, a restriction.
Proper, fitting.

n: If a man feels he isn’t treating his fiancée (or daughter) properly by delaying marriage, and she is getting older, they should marry. It is no sin.

f.w: pass the flower of her age
f.g: Beyond the usual age for marriage.
Interpreted either as his betrothed or as his unmarried daughter.

n: But one who is settled in his decision, under no pressure, and resolves not to marry does well too.

f.w: hath power over his own will
f.g: Has self-control and freedom to choose.

n: Both choices are good, but in the current crisis Paul judges the single path better. The JST reads this as a man who “giveth himself” in marriage.

f.g: In context of the present distress and full-time service, not as a general rule for all ages.

n: A wife is bound to her husband while he lives. If he dies, she may remarry — but only to a believer.

f.g: To a fellow believer.

f.w: as long as her husband liveth

n: Paul thinks a widow is happier remaining single, in his judgment — and he believes he has the Spirit of God in saying so.

f.w: I have the Spirit of God
f.g: Paul gently claims inspiration for his counsel.
